root.name: King's Gambit Declined: Queen's Knight Defense

overview: Black develops the knight instead of taking on f4 or playing ...Bc5 or ...d5. After 3.Nf3 White can transpose to accepted lines if Black takes on f4, or meet ...f5 or ...Nf6 with fxe5. Black aims for quick development and later ...d5 or ...exf4, while White keeps the extra option of d4 and Bc4. I am unsure which reply strong players play after 3.Nf3 and treat this as a loosely defined transpositional line.

white_ideas.idea: 3.Nf3 and Bc4 or d4, building a centre and developing quickly
Keep the gambit option by taking on e5 if Black overreaches
Open the f-file when Black takes on f4

black_ideas.idea: Develop and keep the e5 pawn, then ...d5 or ...exf4

typical_structures.structure: Open Game with the f-pawn gone from f2, e4/e5 locked pawns, tension on f4

character.notes: Declined and loosely defined; the play depends on whether Black takes on f4, and I could not pin it down.

gambit.notes: Declined: no material changes hands in the position; accepted lines transpose elsewhere.

soundness.notes: Sound enough; not a known refutation.

structure.notes: Open Game with tension on f4/e5; open once the f-pawn trades.

approach.notes: Offbeat; the Queen's Knight Defense is seldom chosen by strong players.

level.notes: Positions are open and tactical but unclear in theory.

sublines_that_differ.name: 3.Nf3 exf4
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. f4 Nc6 3. Nf3 exf4
sublines_that_differ.how: Transposes to a King's Gambit Accepted, which is a gambit.

gambit.reason: Declined line; no material changes hands.

structure.reason: The f-file and centre open early.
